post.description:
Reserve a new virtual_machine together with its address within the given network.\
\
The number of cores and the memory of the virtual_machine are taken from the given vm-type. The\
virtual_machine is placed on a random sakura-host, which has enough free cores, memory and\
disk-space for it. The image and the public-key are not set here, but by the following\
create-call.\
\
With `host_uuid` an admin places the virtual_machine on this specific sakura-host instead. The\
request fails with `409`, if the host has not enough free resources or its isolation doesn't\
match `isolated_host`, and with `404`, if the host doesn't exist. Other users are not allowed\
to set `host_uuid`.

disk_size.description: size of the disk of the virtual_machine in GiB

memory_size.description: memory of the virtual_machine; in bytes from sakura, in MiB from hanami

torii_address.description: Address of the sakura-host of the virtual_machine, which is a proxy of the torii at the edge, so it stays the same, when the virtual_machine is moved to another sakura-host. Empty in the responses of sakura itself.

post.description:
Reserve a new virtual_machine for another component, for example to restore it\
from a backup.\
\
It works like the reservation of the users, but the number of cores and the memory in MiB are given\
directly instead of a vm-type. With `uuid`, `internal_ip` and `mac_address` the virtual_machine\
keeps the original values of the backup. A UUID, which is used by an active virtual_machine or by\
another project, or an address, which is already used, is rejected with `409`. The UUID of a\
deleted virtual_machine of the same project can be used again. The values, which are not given,\
are selected like for a new virtual_machine.\
\
This is an internal call, which is protected by the internal api-key.

disk_size.description: size of the disk of the virtual_machine in GiB

memory_size.description: memory of the virtual_machine; in bytes from sakura, in MiB from hanami

torii_address.description: Address of the sakura-host of the virtual_machine, which is a proxy of the torii at the edge, so it stays the same, when the virtual_machine is moved to another sakura-host. Empty in the responses of sakura itself.

vm_state.description: Power-state of the virtual_machine: RESERVED, CREATED, RUNNING, STOPPED, RESTORING or ERROR

get.description: Get information of a virtual_machine from the database.

delete.description:
Delete a virtual_machine.\
\
It is deleted on its sakura-host in the background. A watcher releases its cores, memory and\
disk-space on the host, as soon as the sakura-host has finished the deletion. Its metadata is removed from the database, the\
proxy, which is connected to it, is deleted on the torii and the routes from and\
to the virtual_machine are removed from the gateways of its network, together with its\
packet-filters.

get.description:
Get the sakura-host, which runs a virtual_machine.\
\
Other components, like isekai for the backups, use the internal address of the host to call the\
endpoints of sakura for the virtual_machine directly. The virtual_machine must belong to the\
project of the user, unless the user is an admin.\
\
This is an internal call, which is protected by the internal api-key.

post.description:
Move a virtual_machine to another sakura-host. This can only be done by an admin.\
\
The migration is a cold migration, which runs in the background after the request was accepted:\
the virtual_machine is shut down gracefully on its current host, its disk is transferred directly\
to the target host and it is booted there again, if it was running before. It keeps its UUID, its\
address, its proxy-address and its packet-filters. While it is migrated, it can not be started,\
stopped, deleted or get new packet-filters.\
\
The target host must have enough free resources for the virtual_machine. A virtual_machine on an\
isolated host can only be moved to another isolated host, which is free or isolated for its\
project. A virtual_machine on a shared host can only be moved to another shared host. If the\
migration fails, the virtual_machine is started on its current host again.

post.description:
Create new network.\
\
The traffic between the virtual machines of the network, which run on different hosts, is\
encrypted with IPsec, whose keys the gateways exchange over a MLS-group of the network. With\
`disable_encryption` set, the network gets neither the encryption nor the MLS-group. The flag can't\
be changed after the creation.

get.description: List basic information of all networks from the database.
Get information of a network from the database.

delete.description: Delete a network from the database.

get.description:
List the packet filters of all virtual_machines from the database.\
\
Directions of virtual_machines without a filter are unrestricted and not listed.

Get the packet filter of one direction of a virtual_machine from the database.\
\
A direction without a filter is unrestricted and reported as not found.

delete.description:
Delete the packet filter of one direction of a virtual_machine.\
\
Both include-lists are emptied in one step on the torii of the host of the virtual_machine, which\
puts this direction back into its unrestricted default state.

post.description:
Add ip-ranges to the packet filter of one direction of a virtual_machine.\
\
The include-list starts out empty, which means "every address is allowed". The first entry flips\
that around: from then on only packets are carried, whose address is named by one of the ranges.\
For the `ingress` filter this is the source address of the traffic towards the virtual_machine,\
for the `egress` filter the destination address of the traffic sent by the virtual_machine.\
Entries may be written as a single address, as a subnet in CIDR notation or as an explicit range\
`first-last`, and adding one that is already present is a no-op rather than an error.\
\
The change is forwarded to the torii of the host of the virtual_machine.

delete.description:
Remove ip-ranges from the packet filter of one direction of a virtual_machine.\
\
An entry is identified by the addresses it covers, not by the way it was written down:\
`10.0.0.0/24` and `10.0.0.0-10.0.0.255` remove the same entry. Removing the last range opens this\
direction for every address again. A filter, whose include-lists are both empty, is removed.

post.description:
Add ports to the packet filter of one direction of a virtual_machine.\
\
As long as the include-list is empty every port is allowed. Once it holds an entry, only TCP and\
UDP packets with a matching source *or* destination port are carried - matching either side is\
what lets the answers of an allowed service back through the stateless filter. Traffic without\
ports (ICMP and friends) is not affected by this list; it is governed by the ip-ranges alone.\
\
The change is forwarded to the torii of the host of the virtual_machine.

delete.description:
Remove ports from the packet filter of one direction of a virtual_machine.\
\
Entries are matched by the ports they cover, so `22` removes the single port entry and\
`8000-8100` the range. Removing the last entry opens this direction for every port again. A\
filter, whose include-lists are both empty, is removed.

post.description:
Create new floating_ip.\
\
The floating ip-address is only reserved and not attached to any virtual_machine. If no\
floating ip-address is requested, a free one is selected. If a virtual_machine is given, the\
floating ip-address is attached to it directly. If this attach fails, the reservation is\
released again.

internal_ip.description: Internal IP-address of the attached virtual_machine. Not set, if the floating IP-address is detached.

network_uuid.description: Network of the attached virtual_machine. Not set, if the floating IP-address is detached.

get.description: List basic information of all floating_ips from the database.
Get information of a floating_ip from the database.

delete.description:
Delete a floating_ip.\
\
If the floating_ip is still attached to a virtual_machine, it is detached first, so the\
address is never released while the torii still translates it.

put.description:
Attach a floating_ip to a virtual_machine.\
\
The network and the internal ip-address of the virtual_machine are read from the database and\
the NAT of the floating ip-address is registered in the torii. A floating_ip can only be\
attached to one virtual_machine and a virtual_machine can only have one floating_ip.

Detach a floating_ip from its virtual_machine.\
\
The NAT of the floating ip-address is removed from the torii, but the floating ip-address stays\
reserved, so it can be attached to another virtual_machine again. Detaching a floating_ip,\
which is not attached, has no effect.

post.description:
Register a new sakura-host.\
\
This is called by the sakura-host itself without user-interaction, so it requires\
no token, but is protected by the internal api-key and the registration-key.

An isolated host is only used by the virtual_machines of one project, which is bound to the host\
with its first virtual_machine on it. The isolation can only be changed, while no resources are\
allocated on the host and the host is not bound to a project yet. This can only be done by an\
admin.

get.description: Count the virtual machines, networks and floating IP-addresses of a project, which still exist. It is used by miko to check, if a project is empty, before it is deleted. This can only be done by an admin.

Export the networks, virtual_machines, packet filters and floating ip-addresses\
of a project for a backup.\
\
The virtual_machines are exported with their resources and their address within the network.\
Their disk and their config are exported by sakura. The floating ip-addresses are exported with\
the virtual_machine, which they are attached to. The vm-types are not exported, because they are\
global and not bound to a project. Users, which are not admin, can only export their own project.\
\
This is an internal call, which is protected by the internal api-key.

post.description:
Import the networks, packet filters and floating ip-addresses of a project from\
a backup.\
\
The virtual_machines are not imported here, but reserved like new ones over\
`POST /v1alpha/virtual_machine/internal`. So the networks are imported first, the packet filters\
and floating ip-addresses with a second request, after the virtual_machines were reserved. All\
sections of the request are optional.\
\
- Networks keep their UUIDs, unless the `id_map` gives them a new one. A UUID, which is used by\
  another project, is rejected with `409`. An existing network of the project is rejected with\
  `409`, unless `force` is set, which overwrites it. Its subnet and encryption can only be\
  changed, while no virtual_machine uses the network. A deleted network is restored.\
- Packet filters are applied by the torii of the host of their virtual_machine. An existing\
  filter of the same direction is rejected with `409`, unless `force` is set, which replaces it.\
- Floating ip-addresses are allocated again from the pool and get new UUIDs. The address of the\
  backup is only used, if it is still free. A virtual_machine, which already has a floating\
  ip-address, keeps it.\
\
The virtual_machines of the packet filters and floating ip-addresses, after applying the\
`id_map`, must exist in the project. All conflicts are checked, before anything is changed. The\
quota of the project is not checked here. Users, which are not admin, can only import into their\
own project.\
\
This is an internal call, which is protected by the internal api-key.

Secret.description:
Wrapper around a string, which must not be leaked into logs or error-messages.

`Debug` and `Display` both print `***` instead of the content, so a secret stays hidden even when it is part of a bigger struct, which is logged as a whole. The content is only reachable through `reveal`, which makes every intended access visible at the call-site.
